content.title: WEIRD SIGNS YOU'RE ACTUALLY MISSING A KEY NUTRIENT (NOT JUST TIRED)
facts: **White spots on nails** – Not calcium, usually a sign of low **zinc**, often paired with slow wound healing and a weaker sense of taste.
**Restless legs at night** – An itchy, crawly urge to move your legs can point to low **iron** stores, even if blood counts look 'normal enough.'
**Cracking at the corners of your mouth** – Painful little splits that won't heal often signal low **B12** or **iron**, not just dry weather.
**Muscle twitches under your eye** – Random, random eyelid or calf twitching is a classic quiet sign of low **magnesium**.
**Bruising easily** – Bruises from barely bumping into something can mean low **vitamin C**, which your body needs to build strong blood vessel walls.
**Numbness or pins-and-needles in hands** – A tingling, 'asleep' feeling in fingers or toes is linked to low **B12**, affecting nerve signals over time.
**Brittle, ridged nails that peel** – Thin nails that split in layers often trace back to low **iron** or **biotin**, not just harsh soap.
**Night blindness** – Struggling to adjust when headlights hit your eyes in the dark can be an early sign of low **vitamin A**.
**Muscle cramps and irregular heartbeat flutters** – Both can point to low **potassium**, especially after sweating a lot or cutting carbs hard.

content.caption:
A few of these deserve a closer look. Low **zinc** doesn't just show up as white nail spots — zinc is needed to make the enzymes that repair skin and the taste buds on your tongue, so a deficiency quietly dulls both. **Magnesium** twitches happen because this mineral calms nerve signals to your muscles; without enough of it, nerves misfire and you get that annoying under-eye or calf flutter. And that tingling in your hands tied to low **B12** isn't random either — B12 is essential for the protective coating around your nerves, so when levels drop, nerve signals literally start to short-circuit. Everyone's body is different, so treat these as clues worth checking, not a diagnosis.
